title: MR-guided brachytherapy for ablation of small liver tumors to optimize dose application
summary: MRI has the advantage over image guidance on a computer tomograph (X-ray) that the target (the tumor to be targeted) is displayed more precisely and can therefore be targeted more accurately. This is expected to lead to an improvement in therapy and a reduction in complications. Image-guided interventions on the liver under MRI guidance are routinely performed at our institution. In this study, we would like to investigate in detail whether MRI can achieve improved, or more accurate, irradiation of liver tumors compared to image guidance with computed tomography. In particular, we want to analyze whether a lower radiation exposure of the surrounding liver tissue can be achieved.

interventions.name: The intervention is performed during hospitalization.  After the intervention, patients are followed up by the outpatient clinic of the Department of Radiology and receive an MRI of the liver every 3 months and a CT of the thorax and abdomen every 6 months.
